text: Numerical Methods - MTH3007 Week 8 Task 1 Newton’s root-finding method uses the following iterative formula: xn+1 = xn − f (xn) f ′(xn) and requires one initial guess to start running. Use this to find all the roots of: i) x2 = 612 ii) x3 = cos x Task 2 The secant method uses the following discrete formula: xn+1 = xnf (xn−1) − xn−1f (xn) f (xn) − f (xn−1) and requires two initial guesses to start running. Use this to find all the roots of the same equations: i) x2 = 612 ii) x3 = cos x How many iterations does each method need until the approximate root gets arbitrarily close to the actual root? You can implement a check to see the size of the change from one guess to the next. Task 3 Newton’s method for optimisation uses the second-order Taylor expansion of f (x) around a point xk for some small step size xk → xk+1: f (xk+1) = f (xk) + f ′(xk)(xk+1 − xk) + 1 2 f ′′(xk)(xk+1 − xk)2 Since we are wanting to find extrema, we want to find roots of the first derivative at xk+1. That is, we need to differentiate with respect to xk+1, set the resulting expression to zero, then solve for xk+1 to get the iterative formula.
